description.value: A case-control fMRI study examined food cue-induced BOLD activation in obese and nonobese participants and its associations with BMI and plasma leptin concentration.

spans.text: Herein, we present the first study, to our knowledge, to investigate whether leptin levels are associated with the intensity of mesolimbic reactivity to food cues in obese and nonobese subjects.

We excluded the first 5 images we acquired from our analysis to avoid any artifacts caused by the effects of magnetic saturation. We performed a spatial realignment on the remaining 448 images to correct for head motion. Normalization of the images was accomplished using an echo planar imaging template (Montreal Neurological Institute). The normalized images were smoothed using an isotropic gaussian kernel (8 mm full-width half-maximum).

description.value: SPM5 preprocessing of T2*-weighted fMRI data: the first 5 images were excluded to avoid magnetic-saturation artifacts; the remaining 448 images were realigned for head motion, normalized to an MNI echo-planar imaging template, and smoothed with an isotropic 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

spans.text: an anatomical mask for the ventral striatum

We defined the region of interest as the intersection of 2 a priori derived masks, that is, an anatomical mask for the ventral striatum and a mask for the main effect of the paradigm (food > neutral) built by an Statistical Parametric Mapping t -value map with a threshold of P < .01.

We obtained our binary mask by retrieving a region of interest mask of the ventral striatum from the Brede database ( http://neuro.imm.dtu.dk/services/jerne/brede/ ) and converting it to a binary mask with a threshold of P > .25.
